policy.no_fabrication: Every number entering the manuscript must be produced by a script listed here, executed in this session, with raw output under 04_results/.
policy.on_failure: Diagnose, fix the code or protocol, re-run. Record both the failure and the fix in 08_logs/experiment_log.jsonl. Never report a partial run.
policy.cpu_only: All timing measurements run on CPU only. The venv's torch build has no CUDA, making GPU measurement structurally impossible.
policy.provenance: paths.save_result() stamps every result with hardware, library versions and timestamp.

experiments.name: Baseline reproduction of the submitted results
experiments.objective: Reproduce the submitted headline numbers from the real 03-11/Syn.csv before any change, establishing the control against which every revision result is read.
experiments.protocol: 70/30 temporal split, RF(n=200, max_features=sqrt, class_weight=balanced, seed=42), tau=0.70
experiments.acceptance: Split sizes match exactly, or the deviation is traced to a specific preprocessing decision and documented. Metrics within 0.01 absolute percentage points, or the deviation explained.

experiments.name: Feature-set correctness audit and repair
experiments.objective: Establish empirically that H_ttl is a constant-zero column on real data, quantify the information content of all eight entropy features, replace TTL entropy with source-port entropy, and produce a complete feature specification with exact source columns and bin widths.
experiments.protocol: Per-feature variance, unique-value count, single-feature AUC and mutual information for all 88 features, before and after the repair; full re-baseline after the repair.
experiments.acceptance: H_ttl variance confirmed to be exactly 0. Replacement feature has non-zero variance and non-trivial mutual information. Re-baselined metrics reported alongside the original.

experiments.name: Leakage and dataset-artifact audit
experiments.objective: Determine objectively whether the near-perfect accuracy reflects genuine attack signal or dataset artifacts, and evaluate the model after removing ALL objectively-flagged leaking features, not just the top three.
protocol: Exact-duplicate census within partition and across the train/test boundary.
Near-duplicate analysis by MinHash/LSH over quantised feature vectors, plus nearest-neighbour distance distributions from each test flow to its closest training flow.
Single-feature separability probe: per-feature AUC and single-split decision-stump accuracy for all 88 features; objective threshold defines the leakage-suspect set.
Per-class distribution checks: KS statistic, Jensen-Shannon divergence, detection of class-degenerate fields.
Progressive removal: retrain with top-1, 3, 5, 10, 20 suspects removed, and with the entire flagged set removed.
Controls: temporal-shuffle control and label-permutation control.
experiments.acceptance: Label-permutation control must collapse to chance (macro-F1 near 0.5 on balanced view); if it does not, the pipeline is broken and must be fixed before any other result is trusted. All metrics reported with bootstrap 95% CIs.

experiments.name: Collinearity, redundancy and SHAP attribution stability
experiments.objective: Quantify multicollinearity in the 88-dimensional space, build reduced feature sets, and measure whether SHAP attributions are stable enough to be operationally trustworthy.
experiments.dataset: CIC-DDoS2019 03-11/Syn.csv (stratified subsample for VIF and SHAP)
protocol: Pearson and Spearman correlation matrices; hierarchical clustering on 1-|rho|; representatives at several cut heights.
Variance Inflation Factor for every numeric feature; design-matrix condition number.
Reduced sets at roughly 88 -> 40 -> 20 features; retrain and compare accuracy, macro-F1, PR-AUC and latency.
SHAP stability: top-k Jaccard overlap and Spearman rank correlation of global mean |SHAP| across 10 seeds and 10 bootstrap resamples, and between full and reduced feature sets.
experiments.acceptance: Stability table produced for k in {5,10,20}. Reduced-set performance reported honestly even if it matches the full set.

experiments.name: Precision-recall based threshold selection
experiments.objective: Replace FNR-driven threshold selection with precision-recall analysis appropriate to 99:1 imbalance, and select tau on a validation split only.
experiments.protocol: Chronological train/validation/test. PR curve, average precision and PR-AUC on validation. tau chosen by maximising validation F1 and by meeting a precision target. Test-set operating point reported separately. Threshold sweep re-expressed in precision, recall, F1 and PR-AUC.
experiments.acceptance: No test data touches threshold selection. Both the validation-selected tau and the test operating point are reported.

experiments.name: Evaluation protocol formalisation
experiments.objective: Document and execute a defensible protocol: explicit split definitions, nested cross-validation for hyperparameters, and demonstrable separation of tuning from testing.
experiments.protocol: Nested CV (outer temporal folds, inner grid search) for the RF hyperparameters; report inner-fold selections and outer-fold performance; produce the protocol table for the manuscript.
experiments.acceptance: Selected hyperparameters reported per outer fold; variance across folds reported.

experiments.name: Numerical stability of the rolling entropy engine
experiments.objective: Measure floating-point drift of the incremental entropy update over long streams, quantify its effect on classifier decisions, and establish the correct complexity claim.
protocol: Three variants: naive incremental (paper Eq. 6 form), running-sum S form (the implemented one), Kahan/Neumaier-compensated, plus periodic exact recomputation every R updates.
Drive 10^7 or more admit/evict updates; checkpoint against exact from-scratch float64 and exact rational ground truth.
Report max and RMS absolute drift versus update count.
Report the number of flows whose predicted label changes because of drift - the operationally meaningful quantity.
Measure per-update cost to support an expected/amortised O(1) claim rather than an absolute one.
experiments.acceptance: Drift curves produced for all variants; label-flip count reported; a defensible variant adopted and its overhead measured.

experiments.name: Cross-vector and cross-day generalization
experiments.objective: Test whether a SYN-trained detector transfers to other DDoS vectors and to a different capture day.
experiments.dataset: CIC-DDoS2019 03-11 {Syn, Portmap, LDAP, NetBIOS, UDP, MSSQL}, 01-12 {Syn, UDPLag}
experiments.protocol: Zero-shot SYN -> each other vector; leave-one-vector-out training; cross-day 03-11 Syn -> 01-12 Syn. Bootstrap 95% CIs on FPR and FNR.
experiments.acceptance: Full transfer matrix reported including degradations. Degradation is a finding, not a failure.

experiments.name: Cross-dataset validation with confidence intervals
experiments.objective: Genuine cross-dataset transfer to InSDN and CIC-IDS2017, replacing the repository's synthetic InSDN artifact.
protocol: Documented common feature schema; features absent in any dataset are dropped from all so every transfer is like-for-like.
Zero-shot transfer, in-distribution reference, and joint training for each target.
FPR and FNR with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.
experiments.acceptance: Schema mapping published. A transfer result of exactly 1.0 accuracy is treated as a bug signal and investigated before reporting. The synthetic insdn_transfer.json is deleted from the repository.

experiments.name: Unified CPU-only classical baseline comparison
experiments.objective: A single, fair, CPU-only comparison harness removing the GPU asymmetry and the 10K-balanced versus 2.5M-imbalanced unfairness.
experiments.protocol: Two protocols run for EVERY model: (A) full imbalanced temporal split; (B) identically-applied subsampled protocol. Models: Decision Tree, SVM(RBF), Naive Bayes, XGBoost, LightGBM, Logistic Regression, Random Forest. Same threads, same harness, same machine.
experiments.acceptance: Latency reported as p50/p95/p99, not a single mean. Peak memory recorded. Protocol A and B never mixed in one table.

experiments.name: Deep-learning baselines under the same CPU protocol
experiments.objective: Compare against the modern deep detectors Reviewer 4 named, under exactly the protocol used for the classical models.
experiments.protocol: 1D-CNN, LSTM, Autoencoder (reconstruction-error detector), Transformer encoder, and a GNN over a host-interaction / flow-similarity graph. All CPU-only (torch build has no CUDA). Same splits, same metrics, same latency instrumentation as E1.
experiments.acceptance: Every model trains to convergence or its non-convergence is reported. No model is dropped silently.

experiments.name: ROC and precision-recall curves for all methods
experiments.objective: Produce the baseline ROC curves the paper claims to discuss but never shows, alongside PR curves appropriate to the imbalance.
experiments.protocol: Persist per-model ROC and PR curve points from the E1 and E9 runs; compute AUC and average precision with bootstrap CIs.
experiments.acceptance: Curve data for every model in E1 and E9.

experiments.name: Explanation trigger policy and budgeted SHAP throughput
experiments.objective: Define the explanation trigger formally, measure the bottleneck it causes under 99% attack prevalence, and measure three mitigations.
protocol: Formal trigger: predicted positive AND score >= tau AND admitted by the explanation budget.
Measure sustained end-to-end throughput with no budget (the reviewer's bottleneck scenario).
Mitigation A: episode-level deduplication by alert signature, explaining one representative per episode.
Mitigation B: token-bucket explanation budget.
Mitigation C: asynchronous off-path explanation with a bounded queue and measured drop rate.
Produce a throughput-versus-explanation-coverage frontier.
experiments.acceptance: Frontier curve produced with at least six operating points; queue drop rates reported for the asynchronous variant.

experiments.name: Controller-in-the-loop OpenFlow deployment testbed
experiments.objective: Move the evaluation off pure offline replay into a real OpenFlow control plane, measuring controller CPU, memory, end-to-end latency and QoS impact.
experiments.platform: os-ken (maintained Ryu fork), OpenFlow 1.3, software switch agents over real TCP sockets. Mininet and ONOS are unavailable because hardware virtualization is disabled in firmware on this machine; the substitution is disclosed in the paper and in the response letter.
protocol: Controller application embeds the XAI-SDN detector; switch agents replay CIC-DDoS2019 flows in wall-clock time as packet_in and flow_stats_reply messages.
Measure controller CPU percent and RSS via psutil under benign load and under attack.
Measure packet_in to alert latency and alert to flow_mod latency, reported as distributions.
Measure control-channel message rate and bytes per second.
Run concurrent benign background flows and measure their throughput, latency and loss with the detector enabled and disabled (QoS impact).
experiments.acceptance: Real OpenFlow handshake completes; measurements come from the running controller process, not from a simulation of it.

experiments.name: OpenFlow control-channel capacity analysis
experiments.objective: Answer directly how many novel flows per second a single controller can physically ingest, and what happens at saturation.
experiments.protocol: Sweep offered packet_in rate against the E4 testbed until saturation; measure achieved rate, queueing delay and loss. Evaluate table-miss rate limiting, packet_in subsampling and switch-side aggregation as mitigations. Derive the control-channel byte budget per flow.
experiments.acceptance: A measured saturation point is reported, together with an explicit statement of whether and how 60,000 flows/s is reachable.

experiments.name: TCAM occupancy under aggregation and eviction policies
experiments.objective: Show concretely which flow-rule aggregation and eviction policies keep the flow table inside a bounded TCAM during an attack.
experiments.protocol: Bounded TCAM model driven by the real trace. Aggregation: exact-match, /24 source prefix, /16 source prefix. Eviction: hard timeout, idle timeout, LRU, LFU. Measure table occupancy over time, overflow events, rule-count reduction and the mitigation's effect on detection coverage.
experiments.acceptance: Occupancy time series for every policy combination; overflow events counted; false-eviction cost quantified.

experiments.name: Individual alert case studies
experiments.objective: Demonstrate the practical usefulness of per-decision explanations with concrete worked examples.
experiments.protocol: Select a true positive, a false positive, a false negative and a borderline case from the test partition. For each, record the feature vector, the score, the TreeSHAP attribution vector, the top contributing features and an operator-facing narrative.
experiments.acceptance: Four real cases drawn from actual test predictions, not constructed examples.
